rfm_tuples.R: April 23, 2025 Q1 2025 press release headlined 'Reaffirms Full Year 2025 Guidance' and reaffirmed FY25 adjusted EPS of $24.50 ($1,325M adjusted net income). CEO Joseph Zubretsky publicly endorsed the outlook.
rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for CEO discretionary sales after the April 23 8-K reaffirmation and before the July 7, 2025 guidance-cut 8-K. Cross-check against subsequent disclosure events.

rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO Joseph Zubretsky sold 87,500 shares on April 30, 2025 for $28,005,170 (86,400 @ $320.00 + 1,100 @ $324.70) — SEVEN calendar days after the April 23 'reaffirm guidance' 8-K and ~9 weeks before the July 7, 2025 8-K disclosing 'preliminary' Q2 EPS of $5.50 (vs prior implied ~$6.50) and a FY25 guidance cut from $24.50 to $21.50-$22.50. CEO publicly reaffirmed guidance, sold 18% of his holdings days later at ~$320, then disclosed a guidance cut ~9 weeks later. The October 3, 2025 securities class action (Hindlemann v. Molina) specifically targets disclosures between Feb 5, 2025 and July 23, 2025 — the exact CEO sale window. Class period of Feb 5 - Jul 23, 2025 directly brackets: (a) the April 23 'reaffirm guidance' 8-K, (b) the CEO's April 30 $28M sale, (c) the May 21 director sale by Wolf (named in derivative suit) of $484K, and (d) the July 7 guidance cut. Combined with MOH-01, this is the strongest evidentiary stack against management credibility in this 10-K.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied management-commitment claim: the 10-K and Q1 10-Q maintain that long-term targets and embedded earnings remain intact (11-13% long-term premium revenue growth target; Investor Day May 8, 2026 reaffirmed 2029 outlook).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification) — given the issuer's confidence framing, look for open-market code-P purchases by C-suite into the drawdown to corroborate.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ONLY THREE code-P purchases in 17 months: (1) COO James Woys bought 10,000 shares total on 2025-08-04 ($855,745 + $703,620 = $1,559,365 at ~$155.99 avg) — 12 days after the Q2 earnings (July 23) and ~30 days after the July 7 guidance cut, into the bottom of the first leg down. (3) No CEO, CFO, or other named-officer purchases. The COO's $1.56M is the only meaningful Mode-B confirmation but it's a SINGLE officer at one point in time, vs. asymmetric multi-officer SELLING of $33.0M (14 sale transactions across 7 named insiders) over the same period. Sale-to-purchase ratio = $32.99M / $1.66M = 19.9x.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest-insider partial signal: COO Woys' August 2025 $1.56M open-market purchase was timed AFTER the bad news (post Q2 print and post guidance cut) — clean Mode-A behavior consistent with conviction at the trough. Zoretic's $100K Feb 2026 purchase is symbolic. But the magnitude is dwarfed 20:1 by selling concentrated in the CEO, CFO's office (CLO Barlow), and CAO. The asymmetric sell:buy ratio plus the CEO's pre-guidance-cut timing override the small COO signal. This is the OPPOSITE of the ABG pattern (CEO bought $1M into the drawdown and 10%+ holder reloaded).

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 2026 8-K (April 22, 2026): 'reaffirming the Company's full-year 2026 premium revenue and adjusted earnings guidance.' Q1 10-Q (April 23) MD&A frames Q1 MCR of 91.1% as 'strong operating performance even as we continue to navigate a challenging medical cost environment.'
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check actual Q1 2026 financials and segment MCR vs Q1 2025 to test whether 'strong operating performance' is supported.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 GAAP net income $14M vs $298M Q1 2025 — a -95.3% YoY decline. GAAP EPS $0.27 vs $5.45 (-95%). Operating income $83M vs $433M (-81%). Premium revenue DOWN $456M YoY (-4.3%). Consolidated MCR 91.1% (Q1'26) vs 89.2% (Q1'25) — +190 bps; vs long-term target ~88%, well above. Q1 2026 includes a $93M impairment for the planned 2027 MAPD exit. Even backing out the $93M impairment, pre-tax income ~$122M vs $390M = -69%. Q1 2026 reaffirmed FY26 guidance, but pre-tax margin of just 0.3% means even minor MCR deterioration through the year would push GAAP losses.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Calling Q1 2026 'strong operating performance' when GAAP net income fell 95% YoY is materially misleading framing. The Q1 print is a worst-case quarter and the issuer's own narrative softens that with non-GAAP framing. This is the kind of 'language drift' that the Signal-OS framework flags — disclosures technically correct but emphasis manipulated. Combined with the May 8 Investor Day's 2029 outlook and CLO sale May 11, this is part of the cluster of management-credibility flags.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K and Q1 10-Q both state 'we were in compliance with all non-financial and financial covenants' as of Dec 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given compliance is asserted, look for evidence of covenant pressure (amendments, threshold reductions, waivers).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K + Q1 10-Q Note 7 Credit Agreement; 8-K February 6, 2026)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Six DAYS before the 10-K was filed (Feb 10, 2026), MOH executed a 'First Amendment to Credit Agreement' on February 4, 2026, that TEMPORARILY REDUCED the minimum Interest Coverage Ratio from 3.0:1.0 down to 1.75:1.0 for Q1-Q4 2026, then stepping up to 2.00, 2.50, and 2.75 across 2027 quarters. Original covenant 3.0x. They needed a 42% relaxation of the interest coverage covenant to remain compliant through 2026. Interest expense rose to $192M in 2025 (vs $118M in 2024). 6.50% senior notes issued Nov 2025. Total debt rising while operating income collapsed (Q1 2026 OI $83M vs interest expense $54M = ICR ~1.5x at run-rate, BELOW the new 1.75x threshold before non-cash adjustments).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Major Mode-B catch. The 'in compliance' language in the 10-K and 10-Q is technically true ONLY because the company negotiated a covenant relaxation immediately before filing. This is a classic distressed-issuer move that the deterministic m_source flagged. The need to drop the ICR threshold to 1.75x — and step it up over two years — is a strong indication that management does NOT expect 2026 results to recover materially. This contradicts the 'reaffirm 2026 guidance' framing in the April 22 8-K and the May 8 Investor Day.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'consolidated MCR increased to 91.7% in 2025, compared with 89.1% in 2024, or 260 basis points... The consolidated MCR for 2025 is above our long-term target range.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify segment-level MCRs and the magnitude of the deterioration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Segment MCRs (2025 vs 2024): Medicaid 91.6% vs 90.3% (+130 bps); Medicare 92.4% vs 89.1% (+330 bps); Marketplace 90.6% vs 75.4% (+1520 bps). FY25 net income $472M vs $1,179M = -60%. Diluted EPS $8.92 vs $20.42 = -56%. Marketplace MCR blew out 1,520 bps in a single year — the largest deterioration in the segment's history. ConnectiCare acquisition closed Feb 1, 2025 contributed unfavorable initial MCRs to Marketplace. Premium revenue +11% but operating income collapsed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The disclosure is HONEST — MOH quantifies the deterioration plainly and admits it is 'above our long-term target range.' Signal-OS honesty-alpha framework would normally not penalize this. BUT the magnitude (FY25 EPS -56%, Q1 2026 EPS -95%, all three segments above target) combined with the CEO's pre-disclosure $28M sale and the active securities class action means this is structurally a SHORT story, not a 'distressed but honest' story. The disclosure is the SYMPTOM; the underlying business has structural medical-cost pressure that may not normalize for multiple years (the company itself flags OBBBA reductions of 15-20% on 1.2M Expansion members by 2029).

rfm_tuples.M_value: MAPD product is being exited entirely in 2027. 2025 MAPD: ~117,000 members, $1,566M premium revenue = 25% of Medicare segment. 2026 expected: 80,000 members, $1B premium revenue (premium revenue contraction of $566M from MAPD alone). The company never explicitly says WHY it's exiting MAPD beyond margin pressure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: exiting an entire product line — one acquired through M&A as recently as Bright (2024) — is a major strategic reversal that the issuer discloses but doesn't fully frame. Acquired Bright in 2024 for $295M cash, now writing down $93M two years later while exiting the product entirely. Capital allocation discipline question similar to ABG's chronic franchise-rights impairments, but smaller and one-time vs chronic.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'In April 2025, our board of directors authorized the purchase of up to an additional $1 billion of our common stock... As of February 10, 2026, $500 million remained available.' 8-K Aug 12, 2025: company entered into Term Loan A-2 'to partially fund its previously authorized stock repurchase program as a temporary measure.'
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check buyback execution prices to test capital-allocation discipline given the subsequent drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q4 2025 buybacks: only 1,300 shares (and these were tax-withholding, not open-market). $500M of the April 2025 $1B authorization remained at Feb 10, 2026 — meaning ~$500M was spent earlier in 2025 (Q1-Q3). Q1 2026: no open-market repurchases under the program. Critically, MOH took on TERM LOAN DEBT in August 2025 specifically to fund buybacks 'as a temporary measure' — i.e., levered up to repurchase shares at ~$155-250 just before the broader drawdown. Concurrently CEO and other insiders were SELLING at $300+ in April-May 2025. This is asymmetric: the COMPANY used cash and debt to buy stock at one price level while the CEO sold his personal stake at a 2x higher price level.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital-allocation red flag. CEO sells $28M at $320 → company simultaneously authorizes $1B buyback at $200-280 → company takes on term-loan debt to fund buybacks → stock falls to $140 by Q4 2025 → buybacks stop. This pattern transfers wealth from shareholders (via company balance sheet) to the CEO (via personal monetization). Even if individually legal, the COMPOSITE is a governance flag and was almost certainly part of the rationale for the Taylor derivative suit (12/12/2025).

summary: MOH is the strongest insider-vs-calendar SHORT signal in the forward-test cohort. CEO Joseph Zubretsky sold $28M on April 30, 2025 — seven days after a 'reaffirm FY25 guidance' 8-K (Apr 23) and ~9 weeks before a guidance-cut 8-K (Jul 7) that took FY25 adj EPS from $24.50 to $21.50-22.50. An active securities class action (Hindlemann, filed 10/3/2025) and derivative suit (Taylor, 12/12/2025) target disclosures across the exact CEO sale window. Form 4 tape is asymmetric: $33M of named-officer SELLING vs only $1.66M of buying (20x ratio); the lone offsetting signal is COO Woys' $1.56M August 2025 open-market purchase AFTER the guidance cut. Adding to the stack: Feb 4, 2026 credit-agreement amendment reduced the interest coverage covenant from 3.0x to 1.75x (-42%) six days before the 10-K filed asserting 'compliance,' Q1 2026 GAAP EPS down 95% YoY, all three segment MCRs above target (Medicare 92.4%, Marketplace 90.6%), $1B buyback funded partly with new term-loan debt at the same time the CEO was monetizing. The disclosures themselves are technically honest (the MCR blow-out, MAPD exit, and pending litigation are all quantified), but the COMPOSITE of pre-disclosure CEO selling, framing language that calls a 95% earnings collapse 'strong operating performance,' a buried covenant relaxation, and concentrated post-cutoff CLO/CAO selling collectively constitute a SHORT-tier signal. SHORT-tier.
